thread:
sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects observed on /v1/generate-stream. Error rate spike > 8% in the last 5m. Paging on-call.
priya: I'm on it. seeing a sharp rise in chunked encoding resets from gateways -> upstream 502/524. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/streams/overview — 5xx + client resets correlated with increased avg resp-time.
sam: Confirmed. traces show 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and many client cancellations. Might be backpressure at gateway. 
priya: @lina can you check gateway logs and recent deploys? any NGINX or envoy changes? Also check if batch size or token limits changed in runtime config.
lina: No deploys in last 2 hours. Looking at gateway logs now — seeing a lot of ``"error":"client closed request"`` and ``upstream: http_502"``. Also a few `longpoll` timeouts. Pasting tail:
```
[2026-03-15T17:02:12Z] upstream: 502, client=10.12.3.5, req=/v1/generate-stream, bytes=0
[2026-03-15T17:02:13Z] client disconnected: fd=1024, reason=RST
[2026-03-15T17:02:14Z] upstream prematurely closed connection: seq=4584, sent=3123
```
dinesh: Traces show kernel-level RSTs from our side for some connections, but not all. Could be an out-of-memory or file-descriptor exhaustion on runtime pods. Priya, can you check pod metrics (fd counts, oom_kills, kernel logs)?
priya: Checking now. `kubectl top` looks normal CPU/mem on the runtime pods. But `ss -s` shows lots of TIME_WAIT and connections in CLOSE_WAIT for a subset of pods. Also `dmesg` shows repeated "too many open files" warnings around 17:01:xx for node runtime-12.
sam: That matches. If runtime is hitting ulimit on fds we might be forcibly closing client streams which the gateway interprets as upstream closed -> client sees disconnect. Immediate mitigation: rotate the affected pods (drain/replace) and bump ulimit for runtime containers, and enable fallback non-streaming path for affected customers.
lina: I'm going to trigger a rolling restart of runtime-12 node pool and scale up replicas by +2.
priya: Also enabling gateway read timeout extension to 90s for /v1/generate-stream route to reduce client-triggered timeouts while we stabilize. Command:
```
# extend read timeout
curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood.example/configs/gateway -d '{"route":"/v1/generate-stream","read_timeout":90000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN"
```
sre-bot: deploy-bot started rolling restart: runtime-pool-12, 2 pods at a time. ETA ~8m.
dinesh: We should also flip a config to prefer non-streaming fallback for any requests that error after 2 consecutive streaming failures. Adding an emergency feature-flag: streaming.fallback_on_error = true for prod.
priya: Toggled fallback flag in feature-gate. Also pushed a quick NGINX tweak to increase `worker_rlimit_nofile` to 200k on gateways (propagating via config manager).
sam: Patch logs show a drop in 502s after the first pod rotation and the read_timeout bump. Error rate down to ~2.3% now. Still seeing client cancellations but severity reduced.
lina: Rolling restart done. New pods show much lower fd usage. dmesg no longer shows "too many open files". Good sign.
priya: Customer impact: 8 customers reported increased failed streaming attempts in last hour (support ticket count + number of failed request IDs). Most recovered after fallback to non-streaming responses (latency slightly higher but successful). Sending note to support to triage regen attempts for affected customers.
dinesh: Root cause hypothesis: long-lived streaming connections + fd limits on a small subset of runtime pods causing forced upstream closes; gateway and clients interpret that as disconnects — amplified by gateway timeouts. Fixes: increase ulimit, improve fd reclamation, add streaming fallback, and add autoscale for runtime pod conn counts.
sam: Action items tracked in incident doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/2001112223 — I'll create the postmortem template after this stabilizes. Quick TODOs:
- (priya) validate ulimit bump on infra images and roll out to all pools
- (lina) add monitoring alert for fd usage per pod (>80%)
- (dinesh) add an eval to recreate client cancel pattern and test fallback
- (sam) post-incident customer communication draft for support
priya: Will follow up with a short runbook change: if streaming error rate > 3% and fd usage > 70% for any pod group, start rolling restart + enable fallback.
lina: Any reason to escalate to SE? support is handling now; contact list updated.
sam: No active escalation needed. Keeping this thread open for 2h to confirm stability, otherwise convert to postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Incident status changed to: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Latency spike resolved, error-rate down. Continue watch for 30m.
priya: Closing handoff to oncall-monitoring. If anything flares, reopen thread or page.
